clue.text: Drug game one's seen on social media

parts.note: hash is slang for cannabis resin
the children's chasing game

explanation.surface: Someone posts about drugs and a game online and it gets noticed on social media.
explanation.definitionFit: A hashtag is a keyword label prefixed with # that appears in posts on platforms such as Twitter.

clue.text: That oddball keeps rating setter for setting

indicators.note: keeping something holds it inside, so the other pieces go within
an oddball is eccentric, so the word before it is scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: An eccentric is said to keep rating the crossword setter for the scene he sets.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is a non-officer sailor, and the setter is I, the person who wrote the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment or surroundings where something lives, its setting.

clue.text: Sense indication I'm fed up and tense

parts.note: a sigh signals weariness or exasperation
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Someone senses signs of frustration and stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, the faculty of seeing.

clue.text: Child that's unaffected when upset?

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, and unaffected means it reads the same that way

parts.note: a word that is identical read upwards or downwards

explanation.surface: A child who stays calm when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset suggests a tantrum, but in a down clue it means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child or toddler.

clue.text: Poet's drinks with lots of ice

parts.note: gins are drinks of the spirit
a berg, short for iceberg, is a huge mass of ice

explanation.surface: A poet takes his drinks with plenty of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Allen Ginsberg was an American Beat poet, author of Howl.

clue.text: About to abandon struggling President Grant

indicators.note: something struggling is in disarray, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandoning means leaving out, so the short word for about is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: re means concerning or about; these letters are removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US president named Grant is under pressure as an ally deserts him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Grant' reads as Ulysses S. Grant, but Grant is the definition, as a noun. Remove RE from PRESIDENT and shuffle what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed allowance or payment, such as a grant paid to a student or cleric.

clue.text: Jack handles climbs round peak of Alps

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means reading upward, so the letters run backwards
going round something encircles it, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: a handle is a name or title
the top letter of the mountain range

explanation.surface: A climber grips the holds as he goes round the summit of an Alpine mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is an old nickname for a sailor, as in jack tar.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack, or jack tar, is informal for a sailor, a member of a ship's crew.

clue.text: Information list, better including good pointer

parts.note: an index lists information, as at the back of a book

indicators.note: including something takes it in, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for better

parts.note: finer means of better quality
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A list of data improved by one useful tip.
explanation.definitionFit: The index finger is the forefinger, the digit people use for pointing at things.

clue.text: Cover festival with Queen and Blue

parts.note: Eid is a Muslim festival
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for Queen
blue and down both mean sad or depressed

explanation.surface: A newspaper covers a festival featuring Queen and the boy band Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and Blue look like the names of bands at a festival, but they are a royal abbreviation and a word for sad.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt or bed cover, originally stuffed with eider duck feathers.

clue.text: Makes mean answer, occasionally boring socialites

indicators.note: boring into something drills inside it, so those letters go within the word for socialites

parts.note: debs, short for debutantes, are young society women

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the odd letters of the word

explanation.surface: A rude reply bores the society crowd and makes someone look petty.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower in quality or dignity, to cheapen and so make mean.

clue.text: Basic error from defender perhaps wrapped in British flag

indicators.note: something wrapped in an item is enclosed by it, so the error sits inside the flag phrase

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for British
an own goal, often abbreviated OG, is a mistake typically made by a defender in football
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A defender's blunder is draped in the Union Jack, as if a basic error is being covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: The British flag phrase splits into B and STANDARD, with the own goal tucked between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Bog-standard is British slang for ordinary or unremarkable, so it means basic with no frills.

clue.text: Call little Rose, say, to come back

indicators.note: coming back means returning the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a bud is an undeveloped flower, such as a young rose

explanation.surface: Someone is told to phone their little Rose and ask her to come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' has a capital to suggest a girl's name, but it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To dub someone is to name or call them something, as in giving a nickname.

clue.text: Rejected appeal? How awful for all players!

parts.note: tut is an exclamation of disapproval

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for appeal is turned around

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An orchestra's appeal is turned down and someone despairs on behalf of the whole ensemble.
explanation.walkthrough: The rejected appeal comes after the exclamation in the answer, though the clue gives it first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is the musical direction meaning all performers play together, from Italian for everyone.

clue.text: Foreign article penned by Tony Blair, translated dreadfully

indicators.note: something penned by a person is written inside their work, so the article goes within the name
translating changes words into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: An article by Tony Blair in a foreign paper suffers from a terrible translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Intolerably means unbearably, to an extent too awful to endure, which matches dreadfully.

clue.text: We're told bows are for beautiful objects in the Louvre?

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: bows as in ribbons, said together with are, matches the French pronunciation with its silent final letters

explanation.surface: Someone claims ribbon bows count as fine art objects in a Paris museum.
explanation.walkthrough: In French the x and ts are silent, so the phrase sounds like bows are; the question mark flags the loose definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaux arts is French for fine arts, the kind of beautiful works displayed in the Louvre gallery.

clue.text: Medicine can heal, keeping temperature in check

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the temperature sits within the word for heal

parts.note: to cure is to heal
T is the abbreviation for temperature

explanation.surface: A medicine is said to cure illness while keeping a fever under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In check' completes the surface picture of keeping a fever down and adds only the sense of holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a medicine made by dissolving a drug in alcohol.

clue.text: New pilot carrying piece of luggage after BA fired crew member

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: carrying something holds it, so the remaining letter goes inside the word for pilot

parts.note: an aviator flies an aircraft

indicators.note: someone fired is sent away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: a bag is an item of luggage
taken as written; removed

explanation.surface: A new British Airways pilot carries a bag after the airline sacks a crew member.
explanation.walkthrough: BA looks like British Airways but is just two letters to take out of the luggage word.
explanation.definitionFit: A navigator is the member of an aircraft or ship's crew who plots its course.

clue.text: Like wine, opening couple of Viogniers we obtained from France

indicators.note: the opening couple means just the first two letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: the first two letters of the grape variety
nous is the French word for we

explanation.surface: A wine taster describes Viognier wines brought over from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Viognier is a white grape from the Rhône; 'France' tells you to translate we into French.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinous means relating to or resembling wine, from the Latin vinum.

clue.text: Ex-partner in seedy bar embracing ugly brute with energy

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the last letter is simply added on the end
embracing someone holds them within your arms, so the brute goes inside

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar
an orc is an ugly monster of fantasy fiction
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A former spouse is spotted in a sleazy bar hugging a brutish man full of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorcee is a person whose marriage has been legally ended, hence a former spouse.

clue.text: Drunken villains putting away one litre — they get hammered

indicators.note: someone drunken staggers about, so the letters are jumbled
putting something away removes it from view, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one; removed
L is the abbreviation for litre; removed

explanation.surface: Drunk villains down a litre each, and they end up hammered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammered' plays on its slang sense of drunk; an anvil is literally struck by a blacksmith's hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anvils are the iron blocks on which smiths hammer metal, so they are struck repeatedly.

clue.text: One who won't indulge in acid, according to some

indicators.note: according to some speakers signals going by pronunciation rather than spelling

parts.note: acetic acid is the acid in vinegar, and the adjective is said the same way

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to take LSD at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indulge in acid' suggests the drug, but the acid is vinegar's, and only some speakers make the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascetic practises severe self-discipline, abstaining from pleasures and luxuries.

clue.text: Cynic passes on consuming melon

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so the fruit goes within the phrase for passes on

parts.note: to pass on is to die
the Ogen is a variety of melon

explanation.surface: A sceptic dies after eating melon.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynic with its capital names the Greek philosophical school, not a doubting person.
explanation.definitionFit: Diogenes of Sinope was the most famous philosopher of the ancient Cynic school.

clue.text: 15's instrument not destroyed after onset of storm

indicators.note: the onset is the beginning, so only the first letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the word
extant means still existing, surviving

explanation.surface: A navigator's instrument survives intact after a storm hits.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 refers to 15-down, the crew member who plots a course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sextant is the instrument a navigator uses to measure angles to stars and fix position.

clue.text: Spaceman Buzz Lightyear's head stuck in drain, unfortunately

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside, so that letter goes among the others
something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken

parts.note: the first letter of the toy astronaut's surname

explanation.surface: The Toy Story figure Buzz Lightyear has got his head jammed in a drain.
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz Lightyear is the Toy Story astronaut, so the surface steers you away from the real astronaut.
explanation.definitionFit: Buzz Aldrin was the Apollo 11 astronaut who walked on the Moon after Neil Armstrong.

clue.text: Garlic fried with oil generates a little smoke

indicators.note: frying things in a pan tosses them around, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Garlic frying in oil gives off a little smoke in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarillo is a small thin cigar, so it is a little smoke in the sense of something smoked.

clue.text: Expensive accessory has part that's wrong

parts.note: a role is a part played by an actor
a cross marks an answer as wrong

explanation.surface: A pricey accessory has a faulty component.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolex is a luxury Swiss watch brand, a costly item worn on the wrist.

clue.text: Grassland over ditches outside desert

indicators.note: ditching the outside means throwing away the outer letters of the word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
taken as written, then trimmed

explanation.surface: Pasture lies beyond trenches on the edge of the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like a positional word for a down clue, but it is the word that loses its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave someone is to desert or abandon them.

clue.text: Area bordered by dry ink marking

indicators.note: something bordered by other letters has them on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who does not drink
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A region on a map is outlined by dried ink.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means abstaining from alcohol, not lacking moisture.
explanation.definitionFit: Tat is a short informal form of tattoo, an ink design on the skin.

clue.text: Democrat's jibe, dismissing Republican with zero degrees

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so that one letter is taken out

parts.note: to barrack is to jeer or heckle
R is the abbreviation for Republican; removed
the figure 0 looks like the letter O
BA and MA are university degrees

explanation.surface: A Democrat taunts a Republican for having no academic qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: Barrack, to heckle, is mainly British and Australian; drop one R and add O, BA and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the Democratic Party's US president from 2009 to 2017.

clue.text: The Telegraph's leader dismissed by Time

indicators.note: having its leader dismissed means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a tour is a period of duty, as in a tour of service

explanation.surface: The newspaper's editor is sacked by Time magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader reads as the Telegraph's editor, but it is the first letter of the word for Time.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Telegraph itself, the paper's own possessions are described with the first person plural possessive.

clue.text: Like some luggage in comic film series

definitions.meaning: first meaning: cabin bags small enough to take on a plane
second meaning: the long-running British series of bawdy comedy films

explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films were a British comedy franchise from 1958, with titles such as Carry On Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Carry-on describes hand luggage taken into an aircraft cabin, and also names the film franchise.

clue.text: Realise Parisian is sober

parts.note: to realise a sum is to earn or make it
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Someone discovers that a Parisian is not drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Realise here means to make money, as in realising a profit, not to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and solemn in manner, which is one sense of sober.
